goal: Prototype the intended Alice canonical foundation in FloRA without discarding specialist capabilities or building PE/MFM.
procedure: Map each existing service to its actual responsibility. Preserve graph/vector retrieval, object custody, durable ingress and reconciliation. Select pinned RocksDB TransactionDB for canonical event/state consolidation; require tracked generation checks and synchronous WAL. Isolate the owner-rejected SQLite prototype. Write real native rollback, conflict, snapshot, reopen, checkpoint and process-death tests before the adapter; compile the exact library locally while reviewing native handle ownership.
authority: Owner approved prototyping, rejected SQLite and required the same proposed Alice foundation with responsibility conservation. No canonical cutover, model construction or provider-job change authorized by this record.
validation: Three parallel source/primary-document audits reconciled. SQLite reference had eight component passes after two diagnosed fixture defects (product scope and connection cleanup); those do not validate RocksDB. Six expected missing-module RED assertions preserved. Actual native build and tests remain pending; no behavioral or latency result. Native review identified oversized timeout conversion, constructor cleanup and stale-transaction coverage defects. Five invalid configuration subcases first failed, then passed after input-boundary correction. Native resource and generation cases are written but await the build.
failure_or_lesson: One canonical transaction does not replace all specialist capabilities. Temporal owns real derived-index cleanup, not only a restart probe. A temporary backend pass cannot qualify a different production engine. RocksDB WriteBatch/snapshot alone does not guard read dependencies; the semantic kernel must cover new matching records and all mutation paths. Engine choice is not proof of cognition. Validate numeric configuration before native allocation; construction failure must release partial resources. Stable snapshot visibility is not stale read-dependency validation.
